{{short description|Romanian mathematician}}
[[File:SudanGabriel Zurich1932.tif|thumb|[[Zürich]] 1932]]
'''Gabriel Sudan''' (April 14, 1899 &ndash; June 22, 1977) was a [[Romania]]n [[mathematician]], known for the [[Sudan function]],{{sfn|Sudan|1927}} an important example in the [[theory of computation]], similar to the [[Ackermann function]].{{sfn|Ackermann|1928}}

Born in [[Bucharest]], Sudan received his [[Ph.D.]] from the [[University of Göttingen]] in 1925 for his thesis ''Über die geordneten Mengen'' ("On the theory of ordered sets"), supervised by [[David Hilbert]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=7397}}</ref>  He taught at the [[Polytechnic University of Bucharest]] from 1941 until his retirement, in 1966. 

Sudan constructed the function that bears his name with the same aim as [[Wilhelm Ackermann]]: to solve in the affirmative a problem raised by Hilbert. The Ackermann and Sudan functions  are chronologically the first examples of [[Recursion (computer science)|recursive functions]] which are not [[Primitive recursive function|primitive recursive]].
